1.1.name: Quadratics
content: Discriminant and number of real roots
Equations quadratic in some function of x

1.2.name: Functions
content: Function, domain, range, one-one function, inverse function, composition
Determining one-one functions and finding inverses
Graphical relation between function and inverse
Graph transformations: y = f(x) + a, y = f(x + a), y = af(x), y = f(ax)

1.3.name: Coordinate geometry
content: Forms: y = mx + c, y - y1 = m(x - x1), ax + by + c = 0
Distances, gradients, midpoints, points of intersection

1.5.name: Trigonometry
content: Graphs of sine, cosine, tangent functions
Exact values of sin, cos, tan for 30°, 45°, 60° and related angles
Inverse trigonometric notations: sin⁻¹x, cos⁻¹x, tan⁻¹x
Identities: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ, sin² θ + cos² θ = 1
Solving trigonometrical equations in specified intervals

1.6.name: Series
content: Binomial expansion of (a + b)ⁿ for positive integer n
nth term and sum of first n terms
Sum to infinity of convergent GP

1.7.name: Differentiation
content: Gradient as limit of gradients of chords
Derivative of xⁿ for any rational n
Derivatives of sums, differences, composite functions (chain rule)
Applications: gradients, tangents, normals, increasing/decreasing functions

1.8.name: Integration
content: Integrate (ax + b)ⁿ for any rational n except -1
Volume of revolution about an axis

3.1.name: Algebra
content: Solving equations and inequalities with modulus
Polynomial division by linear or quadratic polynomial
Binomial expansion of (1 + x)ⁿ for rational n, |x| < 1

3.2.name: Logarithmic and exponential functions
content: eˣ and ln x: definition, properties, graphs
Solving equations and inequalities with unknowns in indices
Transforming relationships to linear form for determining constants

3.3.name: Trigonometry
content: Graphs of all six trigonometric functions
Identities: sec² θ = 1 + tan² θ, cosec² θ = 1 + cot² θ
Expansions of sin(A ± B), cos(A ± B), tan(A ± B)
Double angle formulae: sin 2A, cos 2A, tan 2A
Expressing a sin θ + b cos θ as R sin(θ ± α) or R cos(θ ± α)

3.4.name: Differentiation
content: Derivatives of eˣ, ln x, sin x, cos x, tan x, tan⁻¹x

3.5.name: Integration
content: Integration of e^(ax+b), 1/(ax+b), sin(ax+b), cos(ax+b), sec²(ax+b), 1/(x²+a²)

3.6.name: Numerical solution of equations
content: Locating roots by graphical methods or sign change
Using iteration xₙ₊₁ = F(xₙ) to find roots

3.7.name: Vectors
content: Unit vectors, displacement vectors, position vectors
Equation of straight line: r = a + tb
Applications: angles between lines, perpendicularity, foot of perpendicular

3.8.name: Differential equations
content: Formulating differential equations from rate of change statements

3.9.name: Complex numbers
content: Complex numbers: real part, imaginary part, modulus, argument, conjugate
Operations in Cartesian form x + iy
Non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
Polar form: r(cos θ + i sin θ) = re^(iθ)

4.1.name: Forces and equilibrium
content: Vector nature of force, components and resultants
Equilibrium: vector sum of forces is zero
Contact forces: normal and frictional components
Coefficient of friction: F = μR or F ≤ μR

4.2.name: Kinematics of motion in a straight line
content: Distance, speed (scalars) and displacement, velocity, acceleration (vectors)
Differentiation and integration for displacement, velocity, acceleration
Constant acceleration formulae: v = u + at, s = ½(u + v)t, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as

4.4.name: Newton's laws of motion
content: Newton's laws for constant mass under constant forces
Motion of particle vertically or on inclined plane

4.5.name: Energy, work and power
content: Work done by constant force: W = Fd cos θ
Gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy
Power as rate of work done
P = Fv for force in direction of motion
Applications: instantaneous acceleration of car on hill with resistance

5.1.name: Representation of data
content: Measures of central tendency: mean, median, mode
Measures of variation: range, interquartile range, standard deviation
Using cumulative frequency graphs for estimates
Calculating mean and standard deviation from raw or grouped data

5.3.name: Probability
content: Evaluating probabilities by enumeration or calculation

5.4.name: Discrete random variables
content: Expectation and variance formulae for binomial and geometric distributions

5.5.name: The normal distribution
content: Normal distribution as model for continuous random variable
Solving problems with X ~ N(μ, σ²)
Finding P(X > x₁) or related probabilities

paper_6.name: Probability & Statistics 2
paper_6.prerequisite: Assumes knowledge of Paper 5 and Paper 3 content

6.1.name: The Poisson distribution
content: Mean and variance equal to λ
Poisson approximation to binomial (n large, p small)

6.2.name: Linear combinations of random variables
content: Var(aX + bY) = a²Var(X) + b²Var(Y) for independent X, Y
Normal distribution properties for linear combinations

6.3.name: Continuous random variables
content: Probability density function concept and properties
Using pdf to calculate probabilities, mean, and variance

6.4.name: Sampling and estimation
content: Sample mean as random variable: E(X̄) = μ, Var(X̄) = σ²/n
Distribution of X̄ when X is normal
Unbiased estimates of mean and variance

6.5.name: Hypothesis tests
content: Null hypothesis, alternative hypothesis, significance level, rejection/acceptance regions
Tests for binomial and Poisson distributions
Type I and Type II errors
